Since when running with Valgrind, entire game runs very slowly, I think that in one frame both game started and ended and that is why crash happened

The offending line in the example: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/c04dfc1174729781219c257fdd1e379a2f1a1a52/examples/game/alien_cake_addict.rs#L311

```rs
            state.set(GameState::GameOver).unwrap();
```

> I think that in one frame both game started and ended and that is why crash happened

Ah, perhaps this is why the `State` isn't being set properly...

Honestly, I don't see why we need an `unwrap` here at all: we're not using the result for anything.

repository.name: bevy
repository.description: A refreshingly simple data-driven game engine built in Rust

issue.body:
# Objective

Examples should use the correct tools for the job.

## Solution

A fixed timestep, by design, can step multiple times consecutively in a single update.

That property used to crash the `alien_cake_addict` example (#2525), which was "fixed" in #3411 (by just not panicking). The proper fix is to use a timer instead, since the system is supposed to spawn a cake every 5 seconds. 

---

A timer guarantees a minimum duration. A fixed timestep guarantees a fixed number of steps per second.
Each one works by essentially sacrificing the other's guarantee.

You can use them together, but no other systems are timestep-based in this example, so the timer is enough.
